title: Chemical Dosing System

introduction.definition: A chemical dosing system stores a treatment chemical and injects it accurately into a process stream using metering pumps. It typically comprises a storage tank with mixer and level gauge, duty and standby diaphragm metering pumps, suction and discharge lines with calibration column, pulsation dampener and back-pressure valve, all on a bunded skid with a control panel.
applications: Water treatment: chlorine, coagulants, pH control
Alumina: flocculant, antiscalant and caustic dosing
Oil & gas: corrosion inhibitor, methanol injection
key_points: Built from: Diaphragm Metering Pump (module 27) or Plunger Pump (module 26)

classification.configuration: Duty/standby diaphragm metering pumps on bunded skid

introduction.summary: A chemical dosing system injects a measured quantity of chemical (coagulant, chlorine, inhibitor, pH control, odorant) into a process or water line. Chemical is stored in a tank (often with a mixer), drawn through a strainer by a duty metering pump (with a standby), and delivered through a pulsation dampener and back-pressure valve to an injection quill. A calibration column on the suction lets operators measure the actual pump output; a safety relief valve protects the pump and piping; everything sits on a bunded skid to contain spills.

script.narration: This module introduces the Chemical Dosing System.
A chemical dosing system stores a treatment chemical and injects it accurately into a process stream using metering pumps.

It typically comprises a storage tank with mixer and level gauge, duty and standby diaphragm metering pumps, suction and discharge lines with calibration column, pulsation dampener and back-pressure valve, all on a bunded skid with a control panel.

Typical applications include water treatment: chlorine, coagulants, pH control; cooling-water and boiler chemical treatment; alumina: flocculant, antiscalant and caustic dosing; oil & gas: corrosion inhibitor, methanol injection.

script.narration: How the Chemical Dosing System works.
The chemical is prepared in the storage tank and kept mixed by the agitator.
The duty metering pump draws chemical through the suction line.
The diaphragm displaces a set volume each stroke into the discharge line.
The control panel paces stroke rate to the process flow or analyser signal.
The bund contains any leakage.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Chemical Dosing System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Chemical Dosing System.
Check tank level and dosing rate.
Calibrate pumps.
Replace diaphragms and valves.
Inspect tank, mixer and piping for chemical attack.
Watch for over- or under-dosing: process off-spec. Common cause: siphoning, gas lock, worn valves.
Watch for chemical leak: liquid in bund. Common cause: fitting failure, material incompatibility.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
